nodes.title: the Nyrazt signature
nodes.statement: The Nyrazt system concerns objects called naksols. There are exactly 6 of them: wrenpyr, vexlorn, vexnak, glimzam, reldxil, pyrxil. Two operations are written % and <>. One relation is written >-, read as "dominates".

nodes.title: the Nyrazt combination tables
nodes.statement: The value of x % y for every pair of naksols is fixed by the table of the first operation, and likewise for <>. The pairs standing in the >- relation are listed in full.

nodes.title: closure under the first operation
nodes.statement: For all naksols x and y, x % y is again a naksol.

nodes.title: association of the first operation
nodes.statement: For all naksols x, y, z: (x % y) % z = x % (y % z).

nodes.title: commutation of the first operation
nodes.statement: For all naksols x and y: x % y = y % x.

nodes.title: a neutral object for the first operation
nodes.statement: There is a naksol wrenpyr with wrenpyr % x = x % wrenpyr = x for every x.

nodes.title: reversal under the first operation
nodes.statement: For every naksol x there is a naksol y with x % y = y % x = wrenpyr.

nodes.title: cancellation in the first operation
nodes.statement: For all naksols x, y, z: if x % y = x % z then y = z.

nodes.title: closure under the second operation
nodes.statement: For all naksols x and y, x <> y is again a naksol.

nodes.title: association of the second operation
nodes.statement: For all naksols x, y, z: (x <> y) <> z = x <> (y <> z).

nodes.title: commutation of the second operation
nodes.statement: For all naksols x and y: x <> y = y <> x.

nodes.title: a neutral object for the second operation
nodes.statement: There is a naksol wrenpyr with wrenpyr <> x = x for every x.

nodes.title: self combination under the second operation
nodes.statement: For every naksol x: x <> x = x.

nodes.title: reflexivity of the relation
nodes.statement: For every naksol x: x >- x.

nodes.title: antisymmetry of the relation
nodes.statement: For all naksols x and y: if x >- y and y >- x then x = y.

nodes.title: transitivity of the relation
nodes.statement: For all naksols x, y, z: if x >- y and y >- z then x >- z.

nodes.title: comparability of every pair
nodes.statement: For all naksols x and y, at least one of x >- y and y >- x holds.

nodes.title: agreement of the relation with the second operation
nodes.statement: For all naksols x, y, z: if x >- y then (z <> x) >- (z <> y) and (x <> z) >- (y <> z).

nodes.title: the system does not have self combination under the first operation
nodes.statement: It is not the case that: For every naksol x: x % x = x.

verification.domain: every tuple of the carrier the axiom quantifies over
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Take the case x = vexlorn, value = vexnak, read straight from the tables.
The two sides of the claim come apart on that case, so the claim cannot hold for every case.
One counterexample is enough. Note that the claim may still hold for many particular objects; what fails is the universal reading.

nodes.title: the system does not have an absorbing object for the first operation
nodes.statement: There is no naksol z with z % x = x % z = z for every naksol x.

verification.domain: every tuple of the carrier the axiom quantifies over
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Take the case reason = no absorbing element, read straight from the tables.
The two sides of the claim come apart on that case, so the claim cannot hold for every case.
One counterexample is enough. Note that the claim may still hold for many particular objects; what fails is the universal reading.

nodes.title: the system does not have spreading of the second operation over the first
nodes.statement: It is not the case that: For all naksols x, y, z: x <> (y % z) = (x <> y) % (x <> z), and the same on the right.

verification.domain: every tuple of the carrier the axiom quantifies over
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Take the case x = vexlorn, y = wrenpyr, z = wrenpyr, left = vexlorn, right = vexnak, read straight from the tables.
The two sides of the claim come apart on that case, so the claim cannot hold for every case.
One counterexample is enough. Note that the claim may still hold for many particular objects; what fails is the universal reading.

nodes.title: the system does not have the absorption pair
nodes.statement: It is not the case that: For all naksols x and y: x % (x <> y) = x and x <> (x % y) = x.

verification.domain: every tuple of the carrier the axiom quantifies over
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Take the case x = wrenpyr, y = vexlorn, value = vexlorn, read straight from the tables.
The two sides of the claim come apart on that case, so the claim cannot hold for every case.
One counterexample is enough. Note that the claim may still hold for many particular objects; what fails is the universal reading.

nodes.title: the system does not have agreement of the relation with the first operation
nodes.statement: It is not the case that: For all naksols x, y, z: if x >- y then (z % x) >- (z % y) and (x % z) >- (y % z).

verification.domain: every tuple of the carrier the axiom quantifies over
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Take the case x = wrenpyr, y = vexlorn, z = pyrxil, side = left, read straight from the tables.
The two sides of the claim come apart on that case, so the claim cannot hold for every case.
One counterexample is enough. Note that the claim may still hold for many particular objects; what fails is the universal reading.

nodes.title: aztumb naksols
nodes.statement: A naksol x is called aztumb when x % x = x.

nodes.title: naksols that glimvash
nodes.statement: Two naksols x and y are said to glimvash when x % y = y % x.

nodes.title: hobreld collections
nodes.statement: A collection S of naksols is hobreld when x % y belongs to S for every pair x, y drawn from S.

nodes.title: the tufex of a naksol
nodes.statement: The tufex of a naksol x is the collection of naksols y for which x >- y holds.

nodes.title: the muxisk
nodes.statement: The naksol wrenpyr is called the muxisk of the system. It is the unique naksol that leaves every naksol unchanged under %.

nodes.title: the tezka
nodes.statement: The tezka of the system is the collection of naksols that glimvash with every naksol.

nodes.title: the nakumb
nodes.statement: The nakumb is the collection of all aztumb naksols.

nodes.title: the thrapon of a naksol
nodes.statement: The thrapon of a naksol x, written [x], is the smallest hobreld collection that contains x.

nodes.title: a solisk
nodes.statement: A naksol f is a solisk when f >- y holds for every naksol y, that is, when the tufex of f is the whole system.

nodes.title: mornpon naksols
nodes.statement: A naksol x is mornpon when x % x equals the muxisk.

nodes.title: the bralum of a naksol
nodes.statement: A bralum of a naksol x is a naksol y with x % y = y % x = wrenpyr.

nodes.title: the gelvex of a naksol
nodes.statement: The gelvex of a naksol x is the number of naksols in its thrapon [x].

nodes.title: the tezyuk
nodes.statement: The tezyuk of the system is the collection of naksols whose gelvex is largest.

nodes.title: xiltez pairs
nodes.statement: Two distinct naksols x and y form a xiltez pair when x >- y and y >- x both hold, that is, when each lies in the tufex of the other.

nodes.title: the muxisk is the only one of its kind
nodes.statement: There is exactly one naksol e with e % x = x % e = x for every naksol x.

verification.domain: every object paired with every object
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Suppose e and f both leave every naksol unchanged.
Then e % f = f, reading e as neutral on the left.
And e % f = e, reading f as neutral on the right.
So e = f, and the two suppositions describe the same object.

nodes.title: the muxisk lies in the tezka
nodes.statement: The muxisk glimvashs with every naksol.

verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Let e be the muxisk and x any naksol.
Then e % x = x and x % e = x.
So e % x = x % e, which is what it means to glimvash.
Since x was arbitrary, e belongs to the tezka.

nodes.title: a naksol has only one bralum
nodes.statement: For every naksol x there is exactly one bralum of x.

verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Let y and z both be partners of x.
Then y = y % (x % z) = (y % x) % z.
Both bracketed products collapse to the neutral object.
So y = z.

nodes.title: a mornpon naksol is its own bralum
nodes.statement: If x % x is the muxisk then the bralum of x is x itself.

verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Let x be mornpon, so x % x is the muxisk.
That is exactly the condition for x to be a partner of x.
Partners are unique, so no other object can be one.

nodes.title: the tezka is hobreld
nodes.statement: If x and y both glimvash with every naksol, then so does x % y.

verification.domain: every ordered pair drawn from the core
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Let x and y lie in the tezka and let z be any naksol.
Then (x % y) % z = x % (y % z).
Move z past y, then past x, using that each glimvashs with everything.
So x % y glimvashs with z, and the tezka is hobreld.

nodes.title: the thrapon of a naksol is hobreld
nodes.statement: For every naksol x, the collection [x] is hobreld.

verification.domain: every object, then every pair inside its span
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: [x] is built by taking x and closing under %.
Closing under an operation is exactly the sealing condition.
The carrier is finite, so the closure stops after finitely many rounds.

nodes.title: the thrapon is contained in every hobreld collection
nodes.statement: If S is hobreld and contains x, then S contains all of [x].

verification.domain: every sealed collection against every object
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Every member of [x] is reached from x by finitely many applications of the operation.
A sealed S containing x is closed under each of those applications.
So each member of [x] is in S, by induction on the number of applications.

nodes.title: a naksol is aztumb exactly when its gelvex is one
nodes.statement: x % x = x holds if and only if [x] contains x alone.

verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: If x % x = x then {x} is already closed under %.
So [x] = {x} and the gelvex is one.
Conversely a span of one object must contain x % x, which is then x.

nodes.title: the gelvex divides the number of naksols
nodes.statement: For every naksol x, the gelvex of x divides 6.

verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: [x] is a hobreld collection.
Its size is the gelvex of x.
The claim is that this size always divides 6.

nodes.title: the thrapon of a tezka naksol stays in the tezka
nodes.statement: If x lies in the tezka then every naksol of [x] lies in the tezka.

verification.domain: every object of the core, then its span
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: The tezka is hobreld.
[x] is the smallest hobreld collection containing x.
A smallest such collection sits inside any other, and the tezka is one.

nodes.title: the nakumb is hobreld
nodes.statement: If x and y are both aztumb then so is x % y.

verification.domain: every ordered pair drawn from the ridge
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Let x and y be aztumb.
The claim asks whether (x % y) % (x % y) returns x % y.
Whether it does is settled by running the operation table on every such pair.

nodes.title: combining on the left never merges two naksols
nodes.statement: For every naksol a, the assignment x to a % x sends distinct naksols to distinct naksols.

verification.domain: every object translated by every object
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Suppose a % x = a % y.
Cancellation on the left gives x = y.
So the assignment is injective, and being injective on a finite carrier it is onto.

nodes.title: tufexs are nested along the relation
nodes.statement: If y lies in the tufex of x, then the tufex of y is contained in the tufex of x.

verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Let y satisfy x >- y and let z satisfy y >- z.
Transitivity gives x >- z.
So every member of the tufex of y is a member of that of x.

nodes.title: there is at most one solisk
nodes.statement: No two distinct naksols can both be solisks.

verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Let f and h both be floors.
Then f >- h, since h is any object, and h >- f likewise.
Antisymmetry forces f = h.

nodes.title: the system has a solisk
nodes.statement: Some naksol solisks the whole system.

verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Every pair is comparable, so the relation orders the objects into a line.
The claim is that the line has a bottom.
The carrier is finite, so the search over candidates terminates.

nodes.title: no xiltez pairs exist
nodes.statement: No two distinct naksols lie in each other's tufex.

verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Suppose x and y form a tight pair.
Antisymmetry then identifies x with y.
So a tight pair of distinct objects cannot arise.

nodes.title: every naksol lies in the tezka
nodes.statement: Every pair of naksols glimvashs.

verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: The tezka is defined by glimvashing with everything.
The claim is that x % y = y % x for every pair.
That is settled by scanning the table for a pair that disagrees.

nodes.title: where every naksol is aztumb breaks down
nodes.statement: It is not the case that: x % x = x for every naksol x.

verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Take the case x = vexlorn, value = vexnak, read straight from the tables.
The two sides of the claim come apart on that case, so the claim cannot hold for every case.
One counterexample is enough. Note that the claim may still hold for many particular objects; what fails is the universal reading.

nodes.title: some naksol reaches every other
nodes.statement: There is a naksol whose thrapon is the whole system.

verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Compute [x] for each naksol in turn.
The claim is that some gelvex equals 6.
The search runs over finitely many objects, so it settles.

nodes.title: where the relation reads the same in both directions breaks down
nodes.statement: It is not the case that: If x >- y then y >- x.

verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Take the case x = wrenpyr, y = vexlorn, read straight from the tables.
The two sides of the claim come apart on that case, so the claim cannot hold for every case.
One counterexample is enough. Note that the claim may still hold for many particular objects; what fails is the universal reading.

nodes.title: where the muxisk swallows everything breaks down
nodes.statement: It is not the case that: e % x equals the muxisk for every naksol x.

verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Take the case anchor = wrenpyr, x = vexlorn, value = vexlorn, read straight from the tables.
The two sides of the claim come apart on that case, so the claim cannot hold for every case.
One counterexample is enough. Note that the claim may still hold for many particular objects; what fails is the universal reading.

nodes.title: the second operation keeps the tezka intact
nodes.statement: If x and y lie in the tezka then so does x <> y.

verification.domain: every ordered pair from the core
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: The tezka is already hobreld under %.
The second operation is defined on every pair.
The claim is that <> respects the tezka as well.
